device.name: Wyze Cam (via docker-wyze-bridge)
device.notes:
Wyze cameras have NO first-party local API — control is cloud-app only. The community docker-wyze-bridge fills the gap: it authenticates to the Wyze cloud once (to enumerate cameras), connects to each camera over Wyze's TUTK peer-to-peer transport, and re-serves the video LOCALLY as RTSP/RTMP/HLS/ WebRTC. This is a "cloud token to bootstrap, local stream thereafter" case, not fully cloud-free.
BRIDGE PORTS (what the bridge exposes on the LAN): RTSP 8554, HLS/HTTP 8888, WebRTC 8889, web UI 5000. Local stream URL: rtsp://{bridge-ip}:8554/{camera-name}.
AUTH: Wyze cloud credentials required — email/password plus (since May 2024) an API Key + API ID from Wyze — to fetch camera info; media then streams locally via P2P. No special camera firmware is required; some newer firmware degrades remote P2P (local LAN usually still works).

openness.notes: Wyze publishes no local API; the bridge reverse-engineers Wyze's TUTK P2P transport and re-emits local streams. A one-time cloud login (API Key + ID) is required to enumerate cameras — the one target here that is not fully cloud-free.

factory_reset.description: One button, two meanings, separated only by how long it is held — which is exactly the shape that catches people out. Three to five seconds is setup mode, which is what someone changing WiFi networks actually wants and which keeps the camera's identity. Ten seconds is the factory reset. Overshooting the first turns a five-minute job into re-adding the camera from scratch.
factory_reset.effect: Clears the camera's WiFi credentials and its account binding, putting it back to first-run state. Footage on the microSD card is not affected; anything in the vendor cloud is a separate matter.

steps.action: With the camera powered, press and hold the setup button on its base for three to five seconds.
steps.expect: A spoken "ready to connect" prompt and a flashing status light.

procedures.basis: Wyze's support article on factory resetting the Cam v1/v2/v3 and Pan v1.
procedures.name: Setup button held for ten seconds (factory reset)

steps.action: With the camera plugged in, press and hold the setup button on its base for ten seconds.
Release and wait at least thirty seconds for the camera to come back.

cloud.local_alternative: Partial — media streams locally (the bridge prefers a LAN connection) once running, but enumerating the cameras requires a one-time Wyze cloud login (email/password + API Key/ID). There is no fully cloud-free path with stock firmware.

methods.description: Onboard the camera in the Wyze app, obtain a Wyze API Key + API ID, and run docker-wyze-bridge with them; it connects P2P and serves local RTSP/HLS/WebRTC.

steps.action: Onboard the camera in the Wyze app.
Get a Wyze API Key + API ID and run docker-wyze-bridge with them.
Consume the local stream at rtsp://{bridge-ip}:8554/{camera-name}.

setup.notes: The camera is onboarded through the Wyze app (cloud) as normal. Then run docker-wyze-bridge with the account's API Key + API ID + email to expose local streams. There is no account-free path — cloud login bootstraps the camera list.

rejoin.notes: Wi-Fi is reconfigured via the Wyze app; the bridge reconnects P2P afterward.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The bridge ports, the local RTSP URL and the cloud-credential requirement are from the docker-wyze-bridge README.
